::: {.lede}
Setting up an RCT, told through one real project. When demand exceeds available funding,
the selection process becomes an opportunity to learn.
:::

```{=html}

```

## The running example: SMART Romania

EU-funded grants of EUR 15,000 to 100,000 for digital tools, equipment, and services.

```{=html}
<div class="facts">
  <div><div class="k">The programme</div><div class="v">Digitalization grants for micro, small and medium enterprises</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Where</div><div class="v">North-East Romania, run by the regional development agency with World Bank support</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Who is randomized</div><div class="v">1,038 eligible MSMEs, pre-screened via an online application survey</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">The design</div><div class="v">Lottery into a treatment group (grants) and a comparison group</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Outcomes tracked</div><div class="v">Digital adoption (DESI), revenues, profits, employment, productivity</div></div>
  <div><div class="k">Starting point</div><div class="v">Average DESI score of 4.3 out of 12; 67% of firms name lack of finance as their main obstacle</div></div>
</div>
```

### From application to evidence

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Application survey</div>
  <div>Lottery</div>
  <div>Digitalization grants</div>
  <div>Follow-up surveys</div>
  <div>Impact evaluation</div>
</div>
```

::: {.team-note}
**Source**
All facts from the baseline report, "Foundational Digital Market Transformation: An RCT in
North-East Romania" (World Bank, 2024). Still to confirm: the treatment and control split,
and the follow-up survey timeline.
:::

## Randomization has to be designed into your programme from the start

An RCT is not something that can be added to a programme after launch. The comparison
group, the eligibility rules, and the baseline data all have to be settled before the
first grant is awarded.

## Building the eligible pool

```{=html}
<div class="flow">
  <div>Outreach<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:var(--dg-ink-soft)">Social media, radio, and events in 20+ cities</span></div>
  <div>Online applications<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:var(--dg-ink-soft)">About one hour to complete</span></div>
  <div>Automatic screening<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:var(--dg-ink-soft)">Stops as soon as a criterion fails</span></div>
  <div style="background:var(--dg-accent);border-color:var(--dg-accent)">1,038<br><span style="font-weight:400">eligible MSMEs</span></div>
</div>
```

::: {.takeaway}
In SMART Romania, one survey did three jobs: application, eligibility check, and baseline
data collection, all in a single step.
:::

## How many firms do I need?

Once you know who is eligible, the next question is whether enough firms are available to
measure an impact. Three things determine the answer.

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
#### Expected impact

The smaller the effect you expect, the more firms you need to detect it.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Desired precision

More certainty about the answer requires more observations.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Budget and capacity

Every firm in the study needs support, monitoring, and surveys.
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Pool too small? Loosen the eligibility bar, or widen the ranking bins.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="case-band"><b>SMART Romania</b><span>&check; 1,038 eligible firms in the pool</span><span>&check; Built through outreach in 20+ cities</span></div>
```

Rules of thumb and power calculations are covered in
[Advanced How](03-advanced-how.qmd).

## How the lottery worked

With 1,038 firms in the pool and grants for only some, SMART Romania needed a fair way to
choose.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 680 220" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="1038 eligible firms enter a random draw and are split into a treatment group receiving grants and a comparison group receiving none">
  <rect x="10" y="76" width="150" height="66" rx="6" fill="var(--dg-panel)" stroke="var(--dg-rule)"/>
  <text x="85" y="105" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="20" font-weight="bold">1,038</text>
  <text x="85" y="124" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11.5">eligible firms</text>

  <path d="M160 109 H210" stroke="var(--dg-line)" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <rect x="210" y="76" width="160" height="66" rx="6" fill="var(--dg-accent)"/>
  <text x="290" y="102" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">RANDOM DRAW</text>
  <text x="290" y="121" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="11">every firm, the same chance</text>

  <path d="M370 109 H400 V44 H430" stroke="var(--dg-line)" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>
  <path d="M370 109 H400 V174 H430" stroke="var(--dg-line)" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none"/>

  <rect x="430" y="20" width="240" height="50" rx="6" fill="var(--dg-accent)"/>
  <text x="446" y="41" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">Treatment group</text>
  <text x="446" y="58" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="11">Grants of EUR 15,000 to 100,000</text>

  <rect x="430" y="150" width="240" height="50" rx="6" fill="var(--dg-panel)" stroke="var(--dg-rule)"/>
  <text x="446" y="171" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold">Comparison group</text>
  <text x="446" y="188" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11">No grant; surveyed the same way</text>
</svg>
</figure>
```

::: {.takeaway}
In SMART Romania, the draw, and nothing else, decided which firms received support.
:::

::: {.team-note}
**To confirm**
Exact treatment and control split, and whether the draw was public or computerized.
:::

## Public draw or private draw?

::: {.compare}
::: {.col-e}
::: {.col-head}
Public lottery
:::
::: {.body}
A public draw, for example pulling names from a hat.

**Advantage:** transparent and fair.

**Disadvantage:** the comparison group may change its behaviour once it knows the result.
:::
:::
::: {.col-e}
::: {.col-head}
Private lottery
:::
::: {.body}
A lottery run behind the scenes.

**Advantage:** avoids the comparison group reacting to a public result.

**Disadvantage:** less visibly fair.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
In practice, many World Bank-supported evaluations run the draw as a secure, documented,
computerized procedure that can be re-checked afterwards.
:::

## Narrowing the pool: a lottery around a cutoff

Score firms on eligibility criteria. Accept the top scorers outright, reject the bottom
outright, and randomize only the firms in between.

**Best when:** eligibility criteria are clear and the programme is oversubscribed, with
limited resources.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 660 300" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Firms scored from 100 down to 45; the top band is accepted outright, the bottom rejected, and the middle band randomized">
  <text x="20" y="24" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold">Score</text>

  <rect x="90" y="34" width="280" height="56" rx="5" fill="var(--dg-accent)"/>
  <text x="230" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Accept all</text>
  <text x="230" y="78" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="11">top scorers funded outright</text>
  <text x="72" y="42" text-anchor="end" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">100</text>
  <text x="72" y="96" text-anchor="end" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">60</text>

  <rect x="90" y="100" width="280" height="76" rx="5" fill="var(--dg-panel)" stroke="var(--dg-accent)" stroke-width="2" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/>
  <text x="230" y="126" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Randomize this band</text>
  <text x="230" y="145" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11">85% treatment, 15% comparison</text>
  <text x="230" y="163" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11">this band is the sample for study</text>
  <text x="72" y="182" text-anchor="end" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="12" font-weight="bold">45</text>

  <rect x="90" y="186" width="280" height="52" rx="5" fill="var(--dg-panel)" stroke="var(--dg-rule)"/>
  <text x="230" y="210" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">Reject all</text>
  <text x="230" y="228" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11">below the eligibility bar</text>

  <path d="M382 138 H410" stroke="var(--dg-line)" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <rect x="410" y="106" width="230" height="64" rx="5" fill="var(--dg-accent-wash)"/>
  <text x="425" y="128" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold">Only the middle band is randomized</text>
  <text x="425" y="146" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11">The strongest and weakest applicants</text>
  <text x="425" y="160" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11">are handled by the score, not the draw</text>

  <text x="20" y="270" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11.5">Example: credit scoring in the Philippines</text>
</svg>
</figure>
```

::: {.caution}
Keep selection rules-based. Subjective rankings, even by judges or expert panels, have
been shown to introduce hidden bias that a lottery or scored cutoff avoids.
:::

## Why a lottery?

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
#### Fair

In SMART Romania, every eligible firm had the same chance of receiving a grant. Selection
could not be influenced by connections or favouritism.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Defensible

Rules reduce bias. Across several studies, even expert judges struggle to predict which
firms will succeed.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Efficient

One online survey serves as application, eligibility check, and baseline data collection.
:::
:::

::: {.team-note}
**Citations**
For the "defensible" card: Chen et al. (2022) on judicial favouritism in Kenya;
Fafchamps and Woodruff (2017), Identifying gazelles, World Bank Economic Review 31(3);
McKenzie and Sansone (2019), Predicting entrepreneurial success is hard, JDE 141.
Decide whether these belong on the page or in a references section.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span class="on">Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

## What happens after the lottery?

The evaluation now steps back and lets the programme do its work.

::: {.compare}
::: {.col-e}
::: {.col-head}
Treatment firms
:::
::: {.body}
Receive the digitalization grants and put them to work: equipment, software, services.
:::
:::
::: {.col-e}
::: {.col-head}
Comparison firms
:::
::: {.body}
Continue business as usual, without a grant.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Same markets, same conditions, same surveys. The only difference between SMART Romania's
groups is the grant.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span class="on">Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Impact</span></div>
```

## Measuring the programme's impact

While the programme runs, identical surveys continue for treatment and comparison firms
alike: same questions, same timing.

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-e}
#### Digital adoption

Measured with the DESI framework.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Revenue

Turnover and growth over the period.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Employment

Headcount and job creation.
:::
::: {.card-e}
#### Productivity

Output relative to inputs.
:::
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Differences between SMART Romania's firms can now be traced to one cause: the programme.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="tracker"><span>Policy question</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Eligibility</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Lottery</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Program</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span>Follow-up</span><span class="sep">&rsaquo;</span><span class="on">Impact</span></div>
```

## Why randomize?

Now that both groups have been followed over time, the final question is how to attribute
any differences to the programme.

::: {.gold-panel}
**"What would have happened without the programme?"** Randomization makes it possible to
answer this question.
:::

::: {.compare}
::: {.col-e}
::: {.col-head}
Firms drawn in the lottery
:::
::: {.body}
Received digitalization grants.
:::
:::
::: {.col-e}
::: {.col-head}
Firms not drawn
:::
::: {.body}
No grants; surveyed identically.
:::
:::
:::

Because the lottery created two comparable groups, the difference between them is the
true impact of the programme.

## Five practical ways to randomize your programme

SMART Romania used one approach: the lottery. Many programmes need a different design.

```{=html}
<div class="designs">
  <div class="d"><div>
    <h4>Lottery</h4>
    <p><span class="lab">How:</span> randomly select who gets the programme, by public or private lottery.</p>
    <p><span class="lab">Best when:</span> eligibility is clear and the programme is oversubscribed.</p>
  </div></div>
  <div class="d"><div>
    <h4>Multiple treatment arms</h4>
    <p><span class="lab">How:</span> randomly assign different versions of the programme, with or without a control group.</p>
    <p><span class="lab">Best when:</span> you want to know which design works best, not just whether it works.</p>
  </div></div>
  <div class="d"><div>
    <h4>Randomized phase-in</h4>
    <p><span class="lab">How:</span> everyone gets the programme eventually, in a random order. Those still waiting are the comparison group.</p>
    <p><span class="lab">Best when:</span> budget or capacity cannot cover everyone at once.</p>
  </div></div>
  <div class="d"><div>
    <h4>Randomized intensities</h4>
    <p><span class="lab">How:</span> vary how much of the programme a firm gets, for example 100%, 50%, or 0% of eligible employees.</p>
    <p><span class="lab">Best when:</span> spillovers within or between firms are a concern.</p>
  </div></div>
  <div class="d"><div>
    <h4>Encouragement design</h4>
    <p><span class="lab">How:</span> randomize who gets extra outreach to take up the programme, since it cannot be denied to anyone.</p>
    <p><span class="lab">Best when:</span> take-up is voluntary and the programme itself cannot be withheld.</p>
  </div></div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="case-band"><b>SMART Romania</b><span>&check; Used a lottery (design 1)</span><span>&check; Oversubscribed programme</span><span>&check; 1,038 eligible firms</span></div>
```

### Multiple treatment arms

Randomly assign firms to different versions of the programme, plus a comparison group.

**Best when:** you want to know which version works best, not just whether the programme
works. **Trade-off:** the sample is split across more groups, so you need more firms.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">

  <text x="300" y="74" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">3.1</text>
  <text x="300" y="210" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11.5">Version 1</text>

  <rect x="390" y="64" width="90" height="126" fill="var(--dg-accent)"/>
  <text x="435" y="56" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">3.6</text>

  <text x="570" y="25" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="13" font-weight="bold">4.5</text>
```

### Randomized phase-in

Everyone receives the programme eventually, in a random order. Firms still waiting form
the comparison group.

**Best when:** budget or capacity cannot cover everyone at once.
**Trade-off:** long-term impacts cannot be observed.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
```

```{=html}
<div class="case-band"><b>SMART Romania</b><span>&check; Not used: a one-time lottery with a lasting comparison group</span></div>
```

### Randomized intensities

Randomly vary how much of the programme each firm gets, for example 100%, 50%, or none of
eligible employees.

**Best when:** spillovers are likely, for example information spreading between treated
and untreated employees. **Trade-off:** detecting effects at each level needs a bigger sample.

```{=html}
<figure class="fig-e">
<svg viewBox="0 0 660 210" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="Three firms receive the programme at 100 percent, 50 percent and zero percent of eligible employees">
  <line x1="120" y1="165" x2="600" y2="165" stroke="var(--dg-line)" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <rect x="150" y="35" width="110" height="130" fill="var(--dg-accent)"/>
  <text x="205" y="106" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">100%</text>
  <text x="205" y="185" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="12">Firm A</text>

  <rect x="300" y="100" width="110" height="65" fill="var(--dg-accent)"/>
  <text x="355" y="138" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">50%</text>
  <text x="355" y="185" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="12">Firm B</text>

  <rect x="450" y="140" width="110" height="25" fill="var(--dg-muted)"/>
  <text x="505" y="132" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink)" font-size="15" font-weight="bold">0%</text>
  <text x="505" y="185" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="12">Firm C</text>

  <text x="120" y="22" fill="var(--dg-ink-soft)" font-size="11.5">Share of eligible employees within each firm who receive the programme</text>
</svg>
</figure>
```

```{=html}
<div class="case-band"><b>SMART Romania</b><span>&check; Not used: one level of support was compared with none</span></div>
```

### Encouragement design

Low take-up is common even for free programmes. Randomize who gets extra encouragement,
then compare the whole encouraged group with the whole not-encouraged group.

::: {.caution}
Compliance is never perfect. Some encouraged firms never take the programme up, and some
others do anyway. Compare the full groups regardless.
:::

```{=html}
<div class="case-band"><b>SMART Romania</b><span>&check; Not needed: the grants were oversubscribed, so a lottery was possible</span></div>
```
